{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (MSL / IBM)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement, its Attachments, the AECI and the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings**: 13 compliant, 5 deviations requiring redlines, and 1 item that failed verification and needs manual review before it is tabled.

The commercial core of this deal is strongly in our favour and we should protect it. IP ownership sits above the preferred position — Section 13.1 vests outright ownership in IBM of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of delivered Products, with a present and future assignment from MSL — and there is no licence running from MSL to us that could be revoked. The Vendor indemnity in Section 15.1 (IP infringement, procured Parts, deliverables, failure to comply with law) meets the fallback on its material terms with a conventional defence procedure. We carry **no** exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume or liquidated-damages exposure; forecasts expressly do not obligate IBM to purchase, and we may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time. Every audit right in the document runs against MSL, not us. Governing law is New York with a mandatory New York judicial forum and no arbitration. The MSL warranty package (conformance warranty, stated periods in months, repair/replace/refund) sits at the fallback.

The deviations cluster in the exit and risk-allocation provisions. Three of them reach walk-away territory: the **blanket bar on IBM assigning** without MSL approval (no affiliate, successor or M&A carve-out); the **non-renewal notice windows** of six and twelve months, which make the Attachment practically inescapable at term end; and the **liability cap**, set at 3% of bill-of-materials value with **no carve-outs at all**, so that MSL's own indemnity, its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all sit inside a cap far below twelve months' fees. Two further deviations are narrower: the one-sided, over-long non-solicit binding IBM alone, and the absence of any committed post-termination transition assistance or data-export period. Vendor insurance is missing entirely, which matters because MSL holds our consigned inventory and accesses our I/T systems.

One further point is **unverified**: our reviewer flagged the absence of a Customer termination-for-convenience right in a three-year term. That finding failed automated verification and we should not raise it with MSL until the cross-references in Section 5.0 have been re-checked by hand.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity | Meets fallback and most of preferred; no super-cap imposed (favours us). Cap interaction handled under LOL-CAP, not double-flagged. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | Outright IBM ownership by assignment; above preferred. MSL retains only generic production tooling, which the playbook permits. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 16.2 Assignment | Blanket prohibition on IBM assignment with no affiliate or successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard. **Walk-away.** Redline proposed. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | Order-driven; no sole-source or requirements obligation. § 9.0(e) expressly contemplates migration to a competitive supplier. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Delinquency table (§ 2 or more Days delinquent) | No LDs or penalties on IBM; the penalty and profit-rate adjustment mechanics run against MSL. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | Ownership supersedes any licence analysis; affiliate coverage built into the clause 1.9 definition of "IBM". |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Confidentiality "AS IS" provisions | No covenant binds IBM; confidentiality terms expressly preserve freedom to offer competitive products. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review — verification failed** | § 5.0 Termination | Reviewer found no Customer convenience right in a three-year term. **Do not table until manually re-verified.** |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit | All audit rights run in our favour; MSL has none. Better than preferred. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law | New York law, mandatory New York forum, no arbitration. Preferred level. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Attachment 1 | Only MFN runs in our favour ("most favored customer" engineering pricing). Retain. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Attachment 1 | No take-or-pay; forecasts do not obligate purchase; unconditional PO cancellation retained. Requirements-accuracy true-up sits at or above fallback. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 9.0 Personnel | One-sided against IBM, covers all Transferred Employees, runs "[*] years" from the Effective Date. Fails fallback on three material terms. Redline proposed (auto-repaired — see Next Steps). |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (and Attachment § 2.0) | Six-month and twelve-month non-renewal windows; >90 days is **walk-away**. Renewal pricing is fine ("same terms and conditions"). Redline to 60 days. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 5.2 Rights Upon Termination | Assistance gated to expiry/default only, with no committed duration; return limited to documentation and confidential media on a redacted period. Fails fallback. Redline proposed. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 Scope of Warranty | Conformance warranty with repair/replace/refund; sits at fallback. Numeric periods are redacted — confirm commercially. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 13.1 Consigned Products (only insurance reference) | No vendor insurance article; existing references are asset-specific. Fallback (E&O, cyber) not met. New clause proposed. |
| 18 | Low | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15.3 Limitations of Liability | Mutual cap at 3% of bill-of-materials value, well below twelve months' fees, with **no carve-outs**. **Walk-away.** Redline proposed. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three items fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be presented to MSL as such:

1. **§ 15.3 Limitations of Liability (LOL-CAP).** A cap of 3% of bill-of-materials value with no carve-outs means MSL's indemnity under 15.1, its confidentiality obligations under 13.2, and its own gross negligence and wilful misconduct are all capped at a fraction of what we pay. Our ask is the fallback, not preferred: keep the cap mutual, re-base it on twelve months' fees, and add a single carve-out sentence for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **§ 16.2 Assignment (ASSIGN).** A blanket bar on IBM assigning, with no affiliate carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on MSL's approval, fails both the preferred and fallback positions. We propose an IBM affiliate/successor carve-out, confirmation that MSL has no termination right on an IBM change of control, a bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and a reasonableness standard on IBM's approval of other MSL assignments. We are not disturbing MSL's existing consent requirement, which already satisfies the Vendor-consent element.
3. **§ 4.0 Term and Attachment § 2.0 (RENEWAL).** Notice windows longer than 90 days are walk-away; a twelve-month window against a six-month renewal term means the Attachment can effectively never be exited at term end. We propose the minimal fix of sixty (60) days in each clause. Renewal pricing needs no change.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify the termination-for-convenience finding (Item 8) before it goes to MSL.** The finding failed automated verification. The point to check by hand is the interaction of the proposed insertion with the for-cause preamble at Section 5.1 and the Section 4.0 non-renewal notice, so that the cross-reference is not dangling. Hold this item out of the first markup if verification cannot be completed in time.
2. **Re-read the non-solicit redline (Item 13).** The proposed language was auto-repaired, so counsel should confirm the conforming changes read correctly — in particular the replacement of "such Transferred Employees" with "such personnel" and the general solicitation/advertising carve-out. Flag for the business that moving to an involvement-based scope **re-cuts** rather than uniformly narrows the covered population.
3. **Issue the four verified redlines** on assignment (§ 16.2), renewal notice (§ 4.0 / Attachment § 2.0), transition assistance and data export (§ 5.2), and limitation of liability (§ 15.3(b)), plus the new insurance article in the GENERAL section requiring CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy and workers' compensation cover with certificates on request.
4. **Obtain the redacted figures from the business team.** Three findings turn on "[*]" values we cannot see: the Appendix 2 requirements-accuracy percentages and thresholds (confirm they are cost-recovery, not punitive, and that MSL's inventory exposure stays within published lead times and the Supply Flexibility window); the § 19.1 warranty periods for MSL Procured Parts and workmanship; and the § 5.2 a) iii) return period and the § 16.19 survival date for representations and warranties.
5. **Protect the favourable terms.** We should not open § 13.0 (IP ownership), § 15.1 (MSL indemnity), § 7.0 and the Attachment 6 audit rights, the Attachment 1 "most favored customer" pricing, or the § 6.1 PO cancellation right. If MSL raises any of these, our position is that they are settled.
6. **Confirm the change-of-control position expressly.** There is no change-of-control termination right in the document, but nothing affirmatively confirms this; our assignment redline states it, and we should keep that sentence in any compromise draft."}
